An anecdote about the appeal of Apple Watch for regular people

I often see people criticize the Apple Watch saying that it has no practical uses, but I think if most people were to try using the Apple Watch for an extended period of time, many would in fact buy one.

Crap, am I not a regular person for having one? But seriously my favorite thing about it so far is how its changed group social interaction back into what it used to be (almost). When I was out last weekend with friends, I was the only one without my phone on the table feeling the impulse to check it every 30 seconds. If I did have an alert, I didn't have to pull out my phone and have it distract me from the conversation; I just took a quick glance at my wrist and if it wasn't important went right back to the conversation. Even if it does nothing else, I like it for that.

I was amazed when the lead producer for the game announced at E3 that there would be no DLC or microtransactions. I was even more taken aback when he promised the studio would support the game with free content updates for at least a year. That sort of thing is completely unheard of nowadays.

I’m really liking the direction they’re taking Hitman in. Away from the story focus of Hitman: Absolution, back to its roots with individual hits and big levels – and now they even take a step back from Season Passes and paid DLCs while still delivering constant updates and additions. This is going to be interesting and I really hope this model pays off for them.
